input.reasoning:
Backlog totals 214 story points across 24 tasks. With only one rate-card role ("Team member" @ $75/hr, 1 FTE) defined, all effort must be modeled through that single role. I converted story points to hours using a standard heuristic of 8 hours per point (typical for small-to-medium web development tasks with moderate complexity, adjusted upward for known high-complexity items like data migration and payment integration, and downward for lighter admin/config tasks). This gives an aggregate hour estimate per task, summed into a single labour line since only one role exists.

Total story points = 214. Applying ~8h/point average (with internal variance already baked into task-level judgement, though only one role line can be reported) gives ~1,712 hours of engineering work. Since there is only 1 FTE available on the "Team member" role, delivering 1,712 hours sequentially at ~40 hours/week would take about 43 weeks (~10 months) if this one person does everything — design, backend, frontend, QA, DevOps, migration, security, etc. This is a major staffing risk given the breadth of skills required (CI/CD, Angular, RBAC, payments, data migration, i18n/currency, accessibility, observability). I flag this explicitly as an assumption/risk.

Because the rate card only has one generic role, I cannot break hours down by specialty (e.g., "Backend Engineer" vs "QA") — doing so would violate the hard constraint of only using listed roles. So the entire labour estimate is reported under "Team member".

Non-labour costs are estimated separately for third-party/infrastructure costs implied by the backlog: Stripe integration fees/sandbox, staging/cloud infrastructure, observability tooling (tracing/dashboards), and legacy Oracle migration tooling/data transfer costs. These are placeholder estimates pending real vendor quotes.

Priority breakdown: I summed estimated cost per task grouped by priority label, using the same 8h/point conversion at $75/hr.

Scenarios: P50 uses the base 8h/point estimate; P75 adds a 20% contingency for integration/testing overhead typical in fixed-scope backlogs with unknowns (e.g., legacy migration, payment reconciliation); P90 adds a further margin for the significant single-FTE delivery risk and unresolved rate-card/staffing gap.

Reductions: I identified concrete descope/defer opportunities from Low-priority backlog items (support ticket sync, admin back-office, usage analytics, contract tests, legacy decommission) and one scope-reduction on multi-currency (defer PLN support), which collectively could reduce hours meaningfully without threatening the Urgent/High priority core (registration, RBAC, payments, dashboard, migration, GDPR, 2FA, CI pipeline).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration setup, sandbox/test fees, and webhook infrastructure (placeholder)
Staging/cloud infrastructure (CI runners, staging environment hosting) for ~10 months
Legacy Oracle data extraction/migration tooling and temporary storage (placeholder)
Contingency for third-party/legacy helpdesk API access or sandbox fees

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hour with 1 FTE. No real roles (e.g., Backend, Frontend, QA, DevOps) or differentiated rates have been assigned yet, so this estimate is indicative only until the project team is properly staffed and rated.
No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project; all effort figures are derived from story-point-to-hour heuristics, not observed team velocity.

Story points were converted to hours at an average of 8 hours per point, a common heuristic for small/medium web features; high-complexity items (e.g., legacy migration, payment integration) likely have wider variance than this average captures.

With only 1 FTE available on the sole staffed role, the full ~1,712 hours of estimated work (~43 weeks at 40h/week) would need to be delivered sequentially by one person, which is a major delivery-capacity risk given the breadth of skills required (Angular frontend, backend APIs, DevOps/CI, payments, data migration, security, accessibility, observability). This should be treated as a staffing gap, not a real plan.
Non-labour costs (Stripe fees, cloud/staging infra, observability tooling, legacy migration tooling) are rough placeholders pending actual vendor quotes and are not based on confirmed pricing.
Priority breakdown costs are calculated using the same 8h/point conversion and the placeholder rate, summed by each task's declared priority label.
It is assumed all 24 backlog items are in scope for this estimate; no items have been pre-descoped by the client.

scenarios.name: P50 - Base estimate (current backlog, placeholder rate)
P75 - With integration/testing contingency (+20% labour, +10% non-labour)
P90 - With staffing-risk and legacy-migration uncertainty margin (+45% labour, +25% non-labour)

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 Admin back-office for support staff (Low priority, 13 pts) — defer to a later phase; support agents can use direct DB/read-only tools short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes ~104 hours of engineering work from current phase.

reductions.description: Descope PW-19 Usage analytics and reporting (Low priority, 8 pts) — defer CSV export/dashboards until after launch.
reductions.effect: Removes ~64 hours of work; finance can use manual exports temporarily.

reductions.description: Defer PW-23 Contract tests against helpdesk API (Low priority, 5 pts) until after the helpdesk integration has stabilized in production.
reductions.effect: Removes ~40 hours; accepts short-term risk of silent breakage from helpdesk API changes.

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 Decommission of legacy portal (Low priority, 8 pts) until several months post-launch, once the new portal is proven stable.
reductions.effect: Removes ~64 hours from current phase; legacy infra costs continue temporarily.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-14 Multi-currency support scope by launching with only USD and EUR, deferring PLN support (cut ~30% of the 13-point task).
reductions.effect: Removes ~31 hours by narrowing initial currency scope; PLN can be added in a fast-follow release.

reductions.description: Descope PW-12 Support ticket submission sync (Low priority, 5 pts) — customers use existing helpdesk portal directly at launch instead of embedded sync.
reductions.effect: Removes ~40 hours; adds minor friction for customers until sync is built later.

reductions.description: Defer non-labour observability tooling spend until closer to go-live rather than provisioning from project start.
reductions.effect: Delays ~60% of the $2,000 observability tooling cost by several months, reducing early cash outlay.
